correctness.rationale: The nonempty support of a fixed point would contain a whole 5-cycle of adjacent row vertices, so the action is free and simplex interiors have no stabilizers. Orbit CW boundaries use alternating deletion and the sign of the unique translate to the representative. An independent program, replayable as python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_1_2.py 1, enumerated all nonempty vertex masks using a column-major indexing, chose minimum-mask orbit representatives, checked all signed boundary compositions, and reduced each boundary separately by integer unit pivots. The face counts were (20,150,540,1010,1020,590,200,30) upstairs and (4,30,108,202,204,118,40,6) downstairs. Both free-rank vectors were (1,0,0,2,1,0,0,0); the sole nonunit boundary invariant was 5 in degree 2 of the quotient, giving exactly Z/5 in H1. Cokernel torsion of d_(k+1) is the torsion of H_k because their quotient is the free image of d_k. The independent tree-and-triangle presentation eliminated all 131 upstairs generators, so this is the universal cover with deck group C5. Hurewicz and H2=0 give pi2=0 and pi3=Z^2; transfer and the equal third Betti numbers give the identity action rationally and hence integrally on the lattice. In the covering-classifier Serre sequence the only possible incoming differentials to (3,0) would use fiber H^1 or H^2, both zero; a beta(a) is nonzero on BC5, so its pullback is nonzero. On the matching Moore wedge both factors come from the two-dimensional Moore summand, making their product zero. The corrected consequence is non-equivalence to that wedge, not nonexistence of a wedge with the same homology. The source checker was inspected, not executed; the independent program does not compute a cochain-level cup product or repeat the optional direct quotient Tietze route.
